newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico highway, bridge tolls rise 10.2 pct - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico highway, bridge tolls rise 10.2 pct - gov't.

text.p: Mexico's public highway and bridge tolls rose an average 10.21 percent as of Feb. 1 to help finance planned 1997 improvements, the government's roads and bridges authority said in a newspaper announcement Tuesday.

Crossing bridges on the Mexico-U.S. border will now cost 11 pesos for most cars, 28 pesos for two to three axle trucks and two to four axle buses, 60 pesos for four to five axle trucks, 95 pesos for six to nine axle trucks and two pesos for pedestrians, the announcement said.
An approximately two hour ride from Mexico City to the city of Puebla will now cost about 80 pesos for non-commercial vehicles.

"This measure will allow the Road and Bridge Authority to satisfactorily fulfill its modernization, conservation and maintenance programs of 1,115.2 km of highways and 29 national and international bridges," the authority said.
It added that tolls had not risen in eight months, during which inflation rose more than 15 percent.
